subject.title: Cron job `delivered: false` when deliveryBestEffort: true and interim-message guard fires without active subagents

question: Should `delivery.bestEffort: true` override the intentionally retained stale-interim suppression when descendant evidence exists, or should it only bypass the active-descendant wait and early return fixed in the earlier PR?
rationale: The proposed one-line change alters a deliberately preserved delivery policy, while the reported plain no-subagent trigger has not been demonstrated on current main.

options.title: Preserve stale-interim suppression pending trace
options.body: Keep the current policy and first identify the descendant state that reaches the guard; repair only a proven false-positive source.

options.title: Make best-effort always deliver
options.body: Treat best-effort as overriding stale-interim suppression and add focused tests proving that real descendant acknowledgements should be delivered.

recommendation.title: Preserve stale-interim suppression pending trace
recommendation.body: Keep the current policy and first identify the descendant state that reaches the guard; repair only a proven false-positive source.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged best-effort cron-delivery change that preserved the policy under review.
